hook_text: Once ships had steam engines, they no longer had to wait for the wind.
clip_script: A paddle steamer chugs up a river in 1807, smoke pouring from its tall chimney, while sailing boats sit still with empty sails. Then the picture jumps forward. A giant container ship, longer than three soccer fields, glides into Durban harbour. Tugboats push it gently towards the quay. Cranes lift box after box after box. Cars, clothes, phones and machines, all carried across the ocean. Water transport changed, and the world came to our harbours.
visual_style: Whiteboard: a paddle steamer with smoke, a steamship with a propeller, a mail ship, then a huge container ship stacked with boxes and a crane at a quay.
mood: Powerful and proud, like a big ship sounding its horn.
pacing: Old-time chugging start, then a smooth, wide shot of the modern harbour.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the labels on your things to see which country they came from.
